what: The simplified [peer review](#term:merit-review) framework took effect for due dates from January 25, 2025: two factors scored 1 to 9 and a third rated sufficient or insufficient, for most research project [activity codes](#term:activity-code) [39](#cite:39) [41](#cite:41).

[NIH](#term:nih) issued NOT-OD-25-068 announcing a standard 15% [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rate on all [grants](#term:grant) in place of [negotiated rates](#term:nicra) [25](#cite:25). A district court [enjoined](#term:injunction) it on March 5, 2025 and later made the injunction permanent and [vacated](#term:vacatur) the guidance; the First Circuit affirmed on January 5, 2026, holding that the guidance violates the [appropriations](#term:appropriations-act) rider and [HHS](#term:hhs) regulations [24](#cite:24).

The FY 2026 [appropriations act](#term:appropriations-act) (Public Law 119-75) carries section 224, under which the [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) provisions of 45 [CFR](#term:cfr) part 75 continue to apply to [NIH](#term:nih) [grants](#term:grant) [62](#cite:62). The FY 2027 [budget request](#term:budget-request) proposes a [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) on F&A costs for each award [57](#cite:57).

[NIH](#term:nih) announced that [peer review](#term:merit-review) of all applications for [grants](#term:grant), [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement) and R&D contracts would be centralized in the [Center for Scientific Review](#term:center-for-scientific-review); CSR took over first-level review from 23 institute review branches during 2025 [55](#cite:55) [54](#cite:54).

NOT-OD-25-104 stated that [NIH](#term:nih) will not issue awards that include a [subaward](#term:subaward) to a foreign entity, effective on release; direct awards to foreign organizations continue [22](#cite:22). Guidance of July 18, 2025 let institutes convert foreign subawards on ongoing [human subjects](#term:human-subjects) research into separate [supplements](#term:supplement) for the current [competitive segment](#term:budget-period) [101](#cite:101).

NOT-OD-25-155 set out the replacement: a domestic organization submits a PF5 (or UF5) application and each foreign collaborator receives a linked RF2 (or UL2) award [86](#cite:86). [NIH](#term:nih) said competing applications with paid foreign collaborators use the new [grant](#term:grant) type for due dates on or after January 25, 2026; the parent PF5 notice, PA-26-002, was posted January 20, 2026 with a first due date of May 25, 2026 [141](#cite:141) [23](#cite:23).

The 2024 [NIH](#term:nih) Public Access Policy took effect on July 1, 2025, a date set by NOT-OD-25-101 of April 30, 2025; manuscripts accepted on or after that date go to PubMed Central and are public without embargo on the official date of publication [34](#cite:34) [125](#cite:125).

NOT-OD-25-132 limited each [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) to six new, [renewal](#term:renewal), [resubmission](#term:resubmission) or revision applications per calendar year, excluding T codes and R13, and stated that applications substantially developed by AI are not considered the applicant's original ideas; both apply to applications submitted on or after September 25, 2025 [12](#cite:12) [140](#cite:140).

NOT-OD-25-133 required recipient institutions, from October 1, 2025, to train senior/key personnel on [other support](#term:other-support) disclosure and keep a written, enforced policy [128](#cite:128).

A district court judgment of July 2, 2025 declared challenged [NIH](#term:nih) directives and the resulting [grant](#term:grant) [terminations](#term:termination) unlawful and [vacated](#term:vacatur) both; the First Circuit denied a stay on July 18, 2025 [30](#cite:30). On August 21, 2025 the Supreme Court stayed the judgments vacating the grant terminations and left in place the vacatur of the guidance documents, citing the Tucker Act and the Court of Federal Claims [28](#cite:28).

NOT-OD-26-009 updated award terms effective October 1, 2025: an award may be [terminated](#term:termination), to the extent authorized by law, if the agency determines it no longer effectuates programme goals or agency priorities, citing [2 CFR 200](#term:uniform-guidance).340(a)(4); a term a court has [enjoined](#term:injunction) is not enforced against those the order covers [65](#cite:65). The March 2026 [Grants](#term:grant) Policy Statement lists the same ground [139](#cite:139).

The [HHS](#term:hhs) Departmental Appeals Board ruled that it has no jurisdiction under 45 [CFR](#term:cfr) Part 16 and 42 CFR Part 50, Subpart D to hear an appeal of an [NIH](#term:nih) [termination](#term:termination) based on non-alignment with agency priorities, and rejected the appeal [132](#cite:132).

NOT-OD-25-143 announced that from fiscal year 2026 [NIH](#term:nih) no longer posts [notices of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) in the NIH Guide; [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) is the single official source, and the Guide continues for policy and informational notices [9](#cite:9) [10](#cite:10).

[NIH](#term:nih) introduced Highlighted Topics, descriptions of research areas of interest that are not funding opportunities; applications go in through [parent announcements](#term:parent-announcement) or other broad notices [142](#cite:142) [11](#cite:11). NIH reported more than 30 topics posted by March 23, 2026 [90](#cite:90).

[NIH](#term:nih) reported that active funding opportunities fell from over 800 at the start of 2025 to fewer than 500 at the end of 2025, as it shifted toward [parent announcements](#term:parent-announcement) and other broad notices [90](#cite:90).

NOT-OD-25-161 [rescinded](#term:rescission) NOT-OD-25-154 of September 11, 2025, which had announced [NIH](#term:nih) [research security](#term:research-security) policies, and said updated guidance would follow [127](#cite:127) [80](#cite:80).

NOT-OD-26-017 requires senior/key personnel to certify [research security training](#term:research-security) completed within 12 months before submission, for applications due on or after May 25, 2026, implementing section 10634 of the CHIPS and Science Act [33](#cite:33).

NOT-OD-26-018 required the [Common Forms](#term:biosketch) for the biographical sketch and [current and pending (other) support](#term:other-support), prepared in [SciENcv](#term:sciencv) with an [ORCID iD](#term:orcid), for due dates on or after January 25, 2026 [31](#cite:31). A leniency period was extended on February 4, 2026 and ended May 7, 2026; since May 8, 2026 the system rejects submissions without the forms [129](#cite:129) [32](#cite:32).

After the lapse in [appropriations](#term:appropriations-act) that began October 1, 2025, [NIH](#term:nih) cancelled 370 review meetings affecting more than 24,000 applications and changed review practice: 30-35% of applications discussed, a 'competitive but not discussed' middle third, and shorter [summary statements](#term:summary-statement) [126](#cite:126). Notices of April 15, 2026 and September 8, 2026 continued the changes through the January 2027 council round [16](#cite:16) [84](#cite:84).

[NIH](#term:nih) adopted a unified funding strategy effective with the January 2026 council round: institutes do not rely on [paylines](#term:payline), follow six tenets, and publish the factors they weigh; about half of institutes had used paylines before [13](#cite:13) [123](#cite:123) [15](#cite:15).

NOT-OD-26-019 ended [letters of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) and removed the requirement to obtain an institute's agreement before submitting an [unsolicited](#term:unsolicited-request) application requesting $500,000 or more in [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) in any year, effective immediately [37](#cite:37).

[NIH](#term:nih) council slides state that NIH was required to use 50% of remaining competing research project [grant](#term:grant) funds for awards funded in full at the start, from one fiscal year's [appropriation](#term:appropriations-act) [137](#cite:137). The Senate committee's summary of the FY 2026 bill says about 2,000 fewer grants resulted in FY 2025 and describes a new limiting provision; NIH's FY 2026 fiscal notice cites Division B, section 240, which holds FY 2026 obligations for multi-year awards to no more than the FY 2025 amount [63](#cite:63) [21](#cite:21).

The Consolidated [Appropriations Act](#term:appropriations-act), 2026 (Public Law 119-75) was signed February 3, 2026; [NIH](#term:nih) states a program level of $47.5 billion, a 1 percent increase over FY 2025 [21](#cite:21). NIH's notice list shows a notice on a lapse in appropriations dated February 2, 2026, the day before [80](#cite:80).

The [salary limitation](#term:salary-cap) rose to $228,000 (Executive Level II); NOT-OD-26-034 first gave January 11, 2026 as the effective date and NOT-OD-26-038 corrected it on February 9, 2026 to January 1, 2026 [18](#cite:18) [19](#cite:19).

NOT-OD-26-029 ended separate AIDS application due dates, in place since 1988, beginning with applications for the January 2027 [advisory council](#term:advisory-council) round; HIV/AIDS applications use the standard dates [17](#cite:17) [2](#cite:2).

NOT-OD-26-040 ended the requirement to obtain an institute's written permission before submitting a conference [grant](#term:grant) application; the parent R13 notice applies this to due dates on or after April 12, 2026 [97](#cite:97) [52](#cite:52).

NOT-OD-26-046 revised the elements of a [Data Management and Sharing Plan](#term:data-management-plan) and required a new format page for due dates on or after May 25, 2026 [100](#cite:100). NOT-OD-26-100 of July 29, 2026 ended [prior approval](#term:prior-approval) for plan changes from October 1, 2026 and moves active awards to the new format by the FY 2027 [progress report](#term:rppr) [99](#cite:99).

[NIH](#term:nih) published the March 2026 revision of the [Grants](#term:grant) Policy Statement, which folds in Guide notices in effect as of March 17, 2026, supersedes the April 2024 version, and applies to [budget periods](#term:budget-period) beginning in fiscal year 2026 [98](#cite:98) [35](#cite:35).
NOT-OD-26-064 ended the continuous submission policy and restated the two-week late window, effective May 25, 2026 [130](#cite:130).

NOT-OD-26-086 asked for comment, by August 3, 2026, on capping at 2, 3 or 4 the research project [grants](#term:grant) a person may hold at once as [PI](#term:principal-investigator) or [multiple PI](#term:multiple-pi), across 46 [activity codes](#term:activity-code) [89](#cite:89). [NIH](#term:nih) reported nearly 3,300 responses on August 19, 2026 and announced no decision [88](#cite:88).

NOT-OD-26-094 replaces letters of support with letters of collaboration of at most 100 words each, to take effect in fiscal year 2027 with the Forms J [application package](#term:application-package) [131](#cite:131).

NOT-OD-26-088 asks for comment, by October 13, 2026, on a proposal to stop reporting final overall [impact scores](#term:impact-score) and [percentiles](#term:percentile) and to report three categories: 'Most competitive' (top 25%), 'Competitive' (26-50%) and 'Not discussed' (over 50%) [14](#cite:14).

The FY 2027 [President's Budget](#term:budget-request) requests $41.5 billion for [NIH](#term:nih) and proposes merging NIDA and NIAAA, eliminating NCCIH, the Fogarty International Center and NIMHD, moving NIEHS to [CDC](#term:cdc), capping [F&A](#term:indirect-costs) at 15 percent, and funding all competing research project [grants](#term:grant) in full at award [57](#cite:57) [59](#cite:59). The FY 2026 request had proposed consolidating the institutes into eight; NIH's own list still showed 27 [institutes and centers](#term:institute-or-center) on July 7, 2026 [135](#cite:135) [143](#cite:143).

NOT-OD-26-131 states that [NIH](#term:nih) operates under Public Law 119-103, the Continuing [Appropriations](#term:appropriations-act) and Extensions Act, 2027, through December 11, 2026 at the FY 2026 enacted level, and issues non-competing awards below the level on the most recent [Notice of Award](#term:notice-of-award) [83](#cite:83) [61](#cite:61).

[NIH](#term:nih) reported that the research project [grant](#term:grant) [success rate](#term:success-rate) fell from 18.5% in FY 2024 to 13.0% in FY 2025, with applications up from 55,418 to 62,592 and new and [renewal](#term:renewal) awards down from 10,265 to 8,161 [81](#cite:81).

[PAPPG](#term:pappg) 24-1 took effect on May 20, 2024 with the bar on parties to malign foreign talent recruitment programmes, no page limit on the [biographical sketch](#term:biosketch), and synergistic activities as a separate document [250](#cite:250). [NSF](#term:nsf) hosts the government-wide Common Forms for the biographical sketch and [current and pending (other) support](#term:other-support), with a disclosure table of the same date [249](#cite:249).

[NSF](#term:nsf) published its Updates on NSF Priorities page and [terminated](#term:termination) awards it judged not aligned with agency priorities, naming diversity, equity and inclusion, environmental justice, and misinformation and disinformation; it states that appeals will not be reviewed or considered [154](#cite:154). The page was last updated July 24, 2026 and says NSF continues to examine awards [154](#cite:154).

Policy Notice [NSF](#term:nsf) 25-034 capped [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) at 15 percent of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc) on new awards to [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) from May 5, 2025 [237](#cite:237). The District of Massachusetts [vacated](#term:vacatur) it on June 20, 2025 and NSF states it will not implement the policy at this time [238](#cite:238) [237](#cite:237).

A case summary records that [NSF](#term:nsf) [appealed](#term:on-appeal) the judgment on August 14, 2025 and that the First Circuit dismissed the appeal on NSF's own motion on September 30, 2025 [239](#cite:239). NSF awards issued on or after May 5, 2025 still carry a term applying the 15 percent policy if NSF is later permitted to apply it [154](#cite:154).

From June 7, 2025 [PIs](#term:principal-investigator) and co-PIs on [NSF](#term:nsf) awards made on or after May 20, 2024 certify each year that they are not party to a malign foreign talent recruitment programme [247](#cite:247).

The Northern District of California ordered [NSF](#term:nsf), EPA and [NEH](#term:neh) to reinstate [grants](#term:grant) to University of California researchers [terminated](#term:termination) by form letter or under [Executive Orders](#term:executive-order) 14151 or 14173 [240](#cite:240). NSF reinstated 114 awards to 45 institutions as of June 30, 2025, and the Ninth Circuit denied a stay on August 21, 2025 [154](#cite:154) [241](#cite:241).

The Ninth Circuit reversed the [injunction](#term:injunction) for the form-termination class on Tucker Act grounds and affirmed it for the class [terminated](#term:termination) under the DEI [executive orders](#term:executive-order) [242](#cite:242). The government petitioned the Supreme Court for review in August 2026 [243](#cite:243).

In American Association of Physics Teachers v. [NSF](#term:nsf) (D.D.C., 1:25-cv-01923) the court denied a [preliminary injunction](#term:injunction) against NSF's [terminations](#term:termination) on September 10, 2025 [244](#cite:244) [245](#cite:245). A case summary records a partial dismissal on March 25, 2026 and summary-judgment briefing complete on September 3, 2026, with no ruling yet [245](#cite:245).

Important Notice 149, issued July 10, 2025 and effective December 2, 2025, put in place [research security training](#term:research-security) for senior/key personnel, the annual malign-foreign-talent certification, a bar on funding institutions with Confucius Institute contracts, and a revised timetable for the foreign financial disclosure report [247](#cite:247).

[Executive Order 14332](#term:executive-order-14332) requires each agency to have senior appointees review funding opportunity announcements and [discretionary awards](#term:discretionary-grant), to write termination-for-convenience terms into [grants](#term:grant), and to use plain language in announcements [246](#cite:246). [NSF](#term:nsf)'s Supplement 1 cites the order [149](#cite:149).

[PAPPG](#term:pappg) Supplement 1 ([NSF](#term:nsf) 26-200) raised the ceilings for planning proposals to $200,000 per year, RAPID to $300,000 and [EAGER](#term:eager-rapid) to $400,000, set a minimum of two reviewers who may be NSF staff, added a return-without-review ground, and raised the equipment threshold to $10,000 [149](#cite:149).

The [PAPPG](#term:pappg) as printed in 2024 says proposals are reviewed usually by three to ten persons outside [NSF](#term:nsf) [157](#cite:157). Supplement 1 states that full proposals, unless excepted, must be reviewed by at least two reviewers and that review can be conducted internally by NSF staff [149](#cite:149).

[NSF](#term:nsf) announced an organisational realignment to reduce the number of layers; the chart dated 12/14/2025 shows eight [directorates](#term:nsf-directorate) with no divisions beneath them [168](#cite:168) [169](#cite:169). MPS, ENG and GEO state that their divisions became sections, and EDU that its four divisions became two clusters [177](#cite:177) [179](#cite:179) [180](#cite:180) [181](#cite:181).

[PAPPG](#term:pappg) Supplement 2 ([NSF](#term:nsf) 26-202) requires accepted manuscripts in the NSF Public Access Repository at or before publication, removes the 12-month embargo, and requires data supporting publications to be shared at publication [150](#cite:150). From April 27, 2026 the [Data Management and Sharing Plan](#term:data-management-plan) is built with a [Research.gov](#term:research-gov) tool [150](#cite:150).

Congress passed the FY 2026 Commerce-Justice-Science bill with $8.75 billion for NSF on January 15, 2026 [173]. A secondary source reports signature on January 23, 2026, $7.2 billion for Research and Related Activities and $938 million for STEM Education; NSF's FY 2027 request shows FY 2026 enacted as $8,750.00 million [174](#cite:174) [255](#cite:255).

[NSF](#term:nsf)'s FY 2027 request asks for $4,863.15 million, requests $0 for SBE and states that NSF will close out that [directorate](#term:nsf-directorate) in FY 2027, and proposes to move STEM Education into the Research and Related Activities account [255](#cite:255). Its Funding Profile shows a research-grant [funding rate](#term:success-rate) of 18% in the FY 2025 plan and 7% under the request [255](#cite:255).

[NSF](#term:nsf) published for comment a draft Guidance on [Financial Assistance](#term:financial-assistance) to replace the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) (91 FR 38030); comments closed August 24, 2026 [152](#cite:152) [147](#cite:147). NSF's goal is to issue it for use in early to mid FY2027 [151](#cite:151).

[NSF](#term:nsf) issued new [Grant](#term:grant) General Conditions (GC-1) and [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement) conditions dated July 31, 2026 [262](#cite:262). They include articles on [termination](#term:termination), a termination review procedure, the malign-foreign-talent certification and the foreign financial disclosure report [263](#cite:263).

[NSF](#term:nsf) released twelve [Notices of Funding Opportunity](#term:nofo) for foundational research worth over $1.5 billion, in BIO, CISE, ENG, GEO and MPS; most accept proposals at any time [192](#cite:192) [185](#cite:185). They consolidate earlier publications — CBET replaces fourteen programme descriptions, CMMI ten, and BIO Core three [solicitations](#term:program-solicitation) — and none is for SBE, EDU or TIP [197](#cite:197) [199](#cite:199) [192](#cite:192).

SBE programme pages updated in July and September 2026 show no upcoming due dates and state that each programme is waiting for a new publication [224](#cite:224) [226](#cite:226) [225](#cite:225). The CRCNS page carries the same notice [274](#cite:274).

DOE Policy Flash 2025-22 set a standardized 15 percent [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rate for [grants](#term:grant) to [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) [288](#cite:288). The U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts [enjoined](#term:injunction) it on May 15, 2025 and, per DOE's own page, [vacated](#term:vacatur) it on June 30, 2025 [360](#cite:360) [288](#cite:288).

DOE Policy Flash 2026-30 states that PF 2025-22, 2025-25, 2025-26, 2025-27 and PF 2025-38/FAL 2025-05 are no longer in effect as of January 23, 2026, citing Section 313 of H.R. 6938, which requires DOE to apply negotiated [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rates as in fiscal year 2024 [289](#cite:289). An association timeline reports that the First Circuit dismissed the government's appeal on March 16, 2026 [291](#cite:291).

ARPA-E removed a 15% [indirect cost cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) from open notices by modification; in the CATALCHEM-E notice this was Modification 03 of February 6, 2026 [301](#cite:301) [302](#cite:302).

A May 14, 2025 memorandum from the Secretary of Defense and a June 12, 2025 memorandum from the Under Secretary for Research and Engineering capped [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) at 15% on assistance awards to [institutions of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) [293](#cite:293). The District of Massachusetts [vacated](#term:vacatur) the policy on October 10, 2025 [293](#cite:293); plaintiff associations report that the government's appeal was dismissed on February 18, 2026 [292](#cite:292) [291](#cite:291).

[Executive Order 14332](#term:executive-order-14332) requires senior appointee review of funding announcements and [discretionary awards](#term:discretionary-grant) and directs that award terms permit [termination](#term:termination) when an award no longer effectuates programme goals or agency priorities [315](#cite:315). DOE issued an implementing policy flash on February 19, 2026 and NASA changed its award terms on January 14, 2026 [314](#cite:314) [382](#cite:382).

AFOSR's open announcement FA955025S0001 closed on March 23, 2026 with a notice citing [Executive Order 14332](#term:executive-order-14332); proposals sent March 18–23 were to be resubmitted [319](#cite:319). Its successor, FA955026S0001, was posted June 4, 2026 [320](#cite:320).

[Executive Order](#term:executive-order) 14347 authorises 'Department of War' as a secondary title for the Department of Defense and states that statutory references to the Department of Defense remain controlling [348](#cite:348). FY 2026 [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) announcements, the FY 2027 MURI announcement and [DARPA](#term:darpa)'s site use the new title [330](#cite:330) [325](#cite:325) [343](#cite:343).

DOE announced the [termination](#term:termination) of 321 financial awards supporting 223 projects, naming six offices that include ARPA-E; the [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) is not named [308](#cite:308). Recipients had 30 days to appeal [308](#cite:308).
Under the full-year [continuing resolution](#term:continuing-resolution) signed March 15, 2025, [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) received $650 million for 12 programmes in FY 2025 [353](#cite:353).

Under the [appropriations act](#term:appropriations-act) signed February 3, 2026, [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) received $1.27 billion for 34 programmes in FY 2026, including $370.0 million for PRMRP across 52 topics [295](#cite:295).

ROSES-2025 was released on July 10, 2025 rather than in February [372](#cite:372) [294](#cite:294). It made dual-anonymous [peer review](#term:merit-review) the default, removed inclusion plans, solicited fewer programme elements and required [SciENcv](#term:sciencv) biographical sketches [377](#cite:377).

NASA announced on January 23, 2026 that ROSES-2026 would be released in July 2026 [294](#cite:294). On the sweep date a [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) search for NNH26ZDA001N returned nothing and ROSES-2025 received a new programme element on October 2, 2026 [395](#cite:395) [374](#cite:374).

GIC 26-01 revised NASA's award terms: an award may be [terminated](#term:termination) when it no longer effectuates programme goals or agency priorities, and recipients need NASA's authorisation and a written justification for each payment request [382](#cite:382) [381](#cite:381).
GIC 25-02 gives a recipient 30 calendar days from NASA's written notice of intent to terminate to appeal [384](#cite:384).
DOE's [research security training](#term:research-security) certification, set by FAL 2025-02 of October 7, 2024, became mandatory after May 1, 2025 [310](#cite:310).
NASA's [research security training](#term:research-security) certification, set by GIC 26-02 of February 5, 2026, took effect August 5, 2026 [383](#cite:383).

FY 2027 requests against FY 2026 enacted: [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) $7,138,815,000 against $8,250,000,000; ARPA-E $200,292,000 against $350,000,000 [297](#cite:297); NASA Science $3,893.9 million against $7,250.0 million [396](#cite:396); [DARPA](#term:darpa) $5.039 billion against $4.322 billion [343](#cite:343).

DOE's FY 2027 budget brief shows the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy as the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation and the Office of Fossil Energy as the Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office [297](#cite:297).
The ARPA-E eXCHANGE site was decommissioned and its notices moved to the consolidated DOE eXCHANGE; the date of the move is not stated on the notice [305](#cite:305).

A consultant's note says Section 542 of Division A of the FY 2026 [appropriations act](#term:appropriations-act) (H.R. 6938) prohibits NASA, the Department of Commerce and [NSF](#term:nsf) from limiting [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rates [361](#cite:361). The statutory text was not reached in this sweep.
Amendment 0008 moved the proposal deadline of ONR's long-range announcement to 31 December 2026 [334](#cite:334).

The Department of Commerce announced the end of funding under three NOAA [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement) with Princeton University, nearly $4 million, with funding ending June 30, 2025, stating that the awards were no longer aligned with the program objectives of NOAA [450](#cite:450).

DOT announced the [termination](#term:termination) of seven university [grants](#term:grant) totalling $54 million. DOT's list of centres marks grants terminated on May 2, 2025 on the stated ground that the grant "no longer effectuates the program goals or agency priorities" [496](#cite:496) [495](#cite:495).
EPA announced a reduction in force affecting the Office of Research and Development and the establishment of an Office of Applied Science and Environmental Solutions [454](#cite:454).

Secretary's Memorandum 1078-015 set out a USDA reorganization with five hub locations, the end of ARS Area Offices and consolidation of Forest Service research stations in Fort Collins, Colorado. As returned by the fetch, the memorandum does not name [NIFA](#term:nifa) [419](#cite:419).

[Executive Order 14332](#term:executive-order-14332), Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking, was signed (90 FR 38929, August 12, 2025). It requires senior appointee review of new funding announcements and [discretionary awards](#term:discretionary-grant), and directs revisions to the [Uniform Guidance](#term:uniform-guidance) on [termination](#term:termination) for convenience and on [facilities and administrative costs](#term:indirect-costs) [246](#cite:246).

[NIFA](#term:nifa) modified the FY 2026 AFRI Foundational and Applied Science request for applications to extend the application deadline for various programme area priorities, to December 4, 11 and 18, 2025 [404](#cite:404) [424](#cite:424).
DOT opened a re-opened competition for five vacant University Transportation Center slots (one Regional, four Tier 1), with applications due in February 2026 [492](#cite:492) [493](#cite:493).

Secretary's Memorandum 1078-020 named five USDA research and development priorities, effective immediately. [NIFA](#term:nifa)'s FY 2026 notices for Strengthening Agricultural Systems and the Specialty Crop Research Initiative tell applicants that projects are to align with it [418](#cite:418) [412](#cite:412) [414](#cite:414).

[NIFA](#term:nifa) lists a December 2025 version of the USDA General Award Terms and Conditions and a March 2026 version of NIFA's General Terms and Conditions as current; what changed in them was not read [425](#cite:425).

FY 2026 [appropriations](#term:appropriations-act) for NOAA were enacted in H.R. 6938, signed January 23, 2026. NOAA's FY 2027 justification gives FY 2026 enacted discretionary appropriations of $5,634,615 thousand [443](#cite:443) [445](#cite:445).

NOAA's FY 2027 [budget request](#term:budget-request) proposes $0 for the Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research, with research moved to other line offices, and lists [terminations](#term:termination) of Climate Competitive Research, Climate and Ocean Laboratories and Cooperative Institutes, and the National Sea [Grant](#term:grant) College Program. The date given is that of the House hearing on the request [445](#cite:445) [444](#cite:444).

Arnold Ventures issued a [request for proposals](#term:open-call) for causal research on K-12 school policies, with letters of interest due November 13, 2026 and full proposals January 31, 2027 [2321](#cite:2321).

Public Law 119-21 was enacted on July 4, 2025 [2391](#cite:2391). Its tax title includes sections 70415 (endowment excise tax), 70424 (deduction for non-itemisers), 70425 (0.5 percent floor for individuals) and 70426 (1-percent floor for corporations) [2391](#cite:2391).

For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025 the section 4968 endowment excise tax has three rates, 1.4 percent, 4 percent and 8 percent, by student adjusted endowment, and applies to institutions with at least 3,000 tuition-paying students [2390](#cite:2390).

A corporation's charitable contributions are deductible only above 1 percent of taxable income, and up to 10 percent [2392](#cite:2392). Practitioner sources give the effective date as taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025 [2394](#cite:2394) [2395](#cite:2395). Added by slice D: the Joint Committee on Taxation's revenue table for the text the Senate passed on July 1, 2025 gives the same effective date [2497](#cite:2497).

From tax year 2026 individuals who do not itemise may deduct up to $1,000 of cash contributions ($2,000 for married taxpayers filing jointly), with gifts to [donor-advised funds](#term:donor-advised-fund) and [supporting organisations](#term:supporting-organization) shut out [2389](#cite:2389). Individuals who itemise may deduct contributions only above 0.5 percent of their contribution base [2392](#cite:2392).

A federal credit for individuals' cash contributions of up to $1,700 to scholarship granting organisations takes effect January 1, 2027; it requires state participation and IRS-approved lists of organisations [2389](#cite:2389).

The [private foundation](#term:private-foundation) excise tax on net investment income stayed at 1.39 percent; the IRS page updated 11-Sep-2026 gives that rate [2378](#cite:2378). Treasury and the IRS issued Notice 2026-36 (news release IR-2026-73), announcing proposed regulations to come on the section 4960 excise tax, which from taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025 can reach any employee of a tax-exempt organisation paid more than $1 million [2463](#cite:2463).
